questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) The table shows the distribution of marks scored by students in a Mathematics test.

| Marks ($x$) | 1 - 3 | 4 - 6 | 7 - 9 | 10 - 12 | 13 - 15 | 16 - 18 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency ($f$) | 3 | 7 | 15 | 20 | 11 | 4 |

State:

a) upper class boundary of the class $10-12$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The classes are separated by a gap of $1$ mark ($9$ then $10$, $12$ then $13$), so each boundary lies half a unit beyond the class limits.

Upper class boundary of $10-12$: $12+0.5=12.5$.

**Answer: $12.5$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: b) modal class of the distribution.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The modal class is the class with the highest frequency. The largest frequency is $20$, for the class $10-12$.

**Answer: the modal class is $10-12$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Find the:

c) number of students who wrote the test.
d) class mark of each class.
e) mean mark of the distribution to 2 decimal places. *[10 marks for (i)]*

(ii) The functions $f$ and $g$ are defined on the set $\mathbb{R}$ of real numbers by $f:x\mapsto 2x$, and $g:x\mapsto x^{2}$.

a) Evaluate $f(2)$.
b) Express in a similar manner, the function, $gf(x)$. *[5 marks for (ii)]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$gf(x)$ means $g(f(x))$: apply $f$ first, then $g$.

$gf(x)=g(2x)=(2x)^2=4x^2$.

Check with $x=2$: $f(2)=4$ and $g(4)=16=4\times2^2$.

**Answer: $gf:x\mapsto 4x^{2}$.**
